topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning objectives regarding the causes of cancer.

topics.label: Intrinsic and environmental causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual framework of cancer causation by examining the interplay between intrinsic mutational processes and external environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious pathogens drive oncogenesis, illustrated by the case of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which chemical and physical mutagens damage DNA directly or through metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, the initiator-promoter model, and host context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters and host developmental context collaborate with mutational initiators to drive tumor progression.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and proving carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the experimental and epidemiological methodologies used to identify carcinogens and prove their causal link to cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a discussion of personal and societal risk-benefit assessments regarding carcinogenic exposures.
